flashcard_questions.q: How many bars long is Chorus 3 of Africa?
Which new instrument enters in the last bar of each phrase in Chorus 3?
flashcard_questions.a: An electric guitar, playing a new riff.

flashcard_questions.q: How many times is Phrase 3 heard during Chorus 3?
How many solo vocal improvisations are added during Chorus 3?
Which texture is heard in Chorus 3?
Which dynamic marking do the choruses of Africa use?
How many bars long is the Outro in the score?
Which key does the Outro of Africa return to?
What happens to the texture during the Outro of Africa?
flashcard_questions.a: Instruments drop out one by one until only the rhythm track remains.

flashcard_questions.q: How does the recording of Africa end?
Which riff's chords does the Outro repeat?
Why is the structure of Africa described as circular?
flashcard_questions.a: It begins and ends with the same layered percussion.
A structure in popular music where verses alternate with a repeated chorus.

flashcard_questions.q: Where is the unpitched percussion introduction of Africa found?
flashcard_questions.a: Only on the recording, not in the printed vocal score.
Spontaneously creating or varying a melody in real time during a performance.

notes: 15 cards: 5 on the three changes and features of Chorus 3, 5 on the Outro (length, key, texture reduction, fade out, Riff a chords), 1 structural insight (circular form), 1 score-versus-recording card, plus 3 term-to-definition cards (verse–chorus form, vocal improvisation, forte as the chorus dynamic). Phrase 3 is named by number rather than quoted, per the no-lyrics rule. Dropped the exam-technique listening advice — revision strategy is not flashcard content.
